text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: This non-review research paper focuses centrally on land use/land cover (LULC) prediction for the entire country of Jordan, explicitly modeling urban expansion and cropland changes at national scale. It uses spatially explicit, high-resolution land change simulations (LandSHIFT.R) combined with climate and socioeconomic scenarios to generate multiple future scenarios (baseline, FS1-FSD3) with quantitative comparisons of land use area changes and irrigation water requirements. The study provides mapped LULC projections and quantitative metrics (e.g., changes in urban area, cropland area, crop yields, irrigation water demand) for years 2025 and 2050. The workflow integrates climate modeling, crop yield modeling, and land use change modeling with scenario analysis, meeting all core inclusion criteria. The scale is national (Jordan), with spatially explicit modeling, multiple scenarios, quantitative outputs, and accuracy/uncertainty considerations discussed. The primary objective is to analyze and simulate future LULC changes under urbanization, climate, and socioeconomic drivers, fulfilling the central research question of LULC prediction. Therefore, the paper is categorized as OK.
